    <item>
      <title>Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/ebola-swiss-patient-nigeria-dr-congo-concerns-virus-spread</link>
      <description><p>Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda</p><p>Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.</p><p>The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/ebola-swiss-patient-nigeria-dr-congo-concerns-virus-spread">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’</p></li><li><p>Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record</p></li></ul><p>Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/13/f1-returns-to-africa-for-first-time-since-1993-with-10-year-rwanda-deal-from-early-2030s">set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s</a>. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.</p><p>Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b</link>
      <description><p>Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’</p><p>The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.</p><p>It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/missed-opportunity-guinea-bissaus-children-why-trial-frederik-wttde/">wrote</a> on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida</link>
      <description><p>Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">immigration</a> jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.</p><p>Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)</a> facilities in south Florida.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda</p><p>Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.</p><p>The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. <rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines</title><description>Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 01:09:51 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>'The marches went well' – French government on demonstrations a week after looting and violence</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261024-the-marches-went-well-%E2%80%93-french-government-on-demonstrations-a-week-after-looting-and-violence</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands marched across France Saturday protesting the rising cost of living. While demonstrations in Paris started peacefully, they ended with a heavy government security response following escalation. Other cities saw clashes that also contributed to the near-1,000 arrested across the country, meanwhile other countries in Europe rallied over issues with some overlap. "The marches went well" said Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b2132ac-cfe7-11f1-b4e6-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26297483587746.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b2132ac-cfe7-11f1-b4e6-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26297483587746.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">491fcaa6-cfea-11f1-810d-57100c25af8b</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 21:01:56 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b2132ac-cfe7-11f1-b4e6-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26297483587746.jpg">© Thibault Camus, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>France: Watching the Post-Riot Protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261024-france-watching-the-post-riot-protests</link><description>
After the French protests turned into riots last weekend, the curfews, and then the alleged racist mass shooting yesterday on the outskirts of Paris, there has been much anxiety, planning and preparation ahead of today's protests.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6cf47c4c-cfd6-11f1-8f44-bba4eee3dc72/w:1024/p:16x9/MANIF-000-D4BK2PW.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6cf47c4c-cfd6-11f1-8f44-bba4eee3dc72/w:1024/p:16x9/MANIF-000-D4BK2PW.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">929e07dc-cfc8-11f1-ac98-0917a6a15dad</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 18:42:27 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>“Witkoff should step down” says Ukraine Committee Chief</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261024-witkoff-should-step-down-says-ukraine-committee-chief</link><description>
Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted front-line operations for more than a week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4dfa67ae-cfd9-11f1-8261-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/WITKOFF-000-D3XU3NQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4dfa67ae-cfd9-11f1-8261-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/WITKOFF-000-D3XU3NQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e57a472c-cfcd-11f1-84d5-89552613470f</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 18:37:05 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Thousands take to Tel Aviv's streets for protests against Netanyahu</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261024-thousands-take-to-tel-aviv-streets-for-protests-against-netanyahu</link><description>
Thousands marched against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government in Tel Aviv on Saturday – just three days before Israel's general election – demanding accountability for the failure to prevent a Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, that led to the war in Gaza.  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/234bdf36-cfd6-11f1-80cc-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4BH8JA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/234bdf36-cfd6-11f1-80cc-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4BH8JA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">930c3626-cfd2-11f1-8b5f-e72073f9c894</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 18:21:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/234bdf36-cfd6-11f1-80cc-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4BH8JA.jpg">© Jack Guez, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Yemen's Houthi rebels claim new attacks on oil facilities and airports across Saudi Arabia</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261024-yemen-s-houthi-rebels-claim-new-attacks-on-oil-facilities-and-airports-across-saudi-arabia</link><description>

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space ]]>

On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space.

While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before.

The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth.

Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film. When they saw the images for the first time, the scientists were literally jumping up and down with joy.

How it mattered

The ability to photograph Earth from space drove both an expanded interest to continue pushing into space and led to unexpected societal changes with regards to how humanity considered its home planet.

For military and intelligence agencies, the potential now existed for reconnaissance at a far larger scale than what was possible with high-altitude aircraft. That capability expanded to agriculture and meteorological purposes, eventually making Earth observation one of the most common reasons satellites and space stations are deployed into orbit today.

Earth photography from space also gave birth to the environmental movement, as people began to see the planet differently. The fragility of this orb became more apparent, as now Earth appeared a "blue marble" set against an endless black void.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks ]]> It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of "Star Trek" before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.

You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say.

That should trouble any Trekkie. "Star Trek" — a show built on progressive ideals, thoughtful characters, and boundary-breaking television — was completely and totally afraid to say anything at all.

Mash it up, Scotty

To be clear, "Star Trek" is no stranger to genre mashups, and they're not inherently a bad thing. Trek has been running for nearly 1,000 total episodes, and they've been doing mashups since the very first season of "Star Trek: The Original Series", which featured gangster, historical fiction, and war-themed episodes.

The holodeck took things further, giving the writers an excuse to set the action anywhere they could dream up. No more alien planets that look suspiciously like Earth were necessary to completely flip the series’ genre; just work up a hologram malfunction and suddenly "Trek" is a Sherlock Holmes-esque mystery or a noir thriller. And even without the holodeck, genres are fluid things that often take from each other to tell stories within each other’s realms.

But while "Trek" has always dabbled, it's never done an entire season of genre episodes… in fact, that might be unprecedented in all of science fiction TV itself, let alone "Star Trek". This season of "SNW" didn’t use occasional gimmicks to take a break from space fare; it was all gimmick, all the time.

Check out the episode rundown below:

  • Episode 1: Dinosaur adventure/western (Land of the Lost)
  • Episode 2: Space horror (Event Horizon)
  • Episode 3: Raunchy comedy (The Hangover)
  • Episode 4: Wartime drama (Casablanca)*
  • Episode 5: Puppets (The Muppets)
  • Episode 6: Disaster movie/real-time story (The Poseidon Adventure)
  • Episode 7: Soap opera (Days of Our Lives)
  • Episode 8: Cold War film/submarine movie (The Hunt for Red October)
  • Episode 9: Fairytale fantasy (Anything with a dragon)
  • Episode 10: Star Trek (Yes, this episode was basically SNW mashing up with TOS, and we're counting that).

* Some of you are screaming that Episode 4 was a noir. It was not. Not everything in black and white with fedoras is noir.

"Strange New Worlds" season 4 was genre-blending at scale. This wasn’t a hint of another genre influencing the episode; it was full-blown immersion into each and every one.

In the past, when other genres have come into "Trek", the series still felt tonally consistent; the characters never bent to the will of the genre, and its direction stayed the same. That was not true of this season. Characters, directorial style, and tone all bent to the will of the selected genre instead of fitting into the already established universe. There were multiple episodes this season that felt nothing like a "Star Trek" episode.

Also — and I may be in the minority here — there were only two episodes this season that I’d argue were executed well (Episode 6 and Episode 8), meaning that the relentless gimmicks paraded out each week felt not just detrimental to the show itself, but they weren’t much fun to watch either.

To go where everyone has gone before

The real question that crops up from this season is why they did it at all. If you listen to the show’s producers, it’s because they love "Trek" so much and they thought it would help move the characters along.

"I really do respect and hear the criticism that: 'When you have 10 episodes [per season], should they be more homogeneous?’”, co-showrunner and executive producer Akiva Goldsman told TV Line when addressing the criticisms for the season. “For us, the answer was no, because the original series always jumped around in genre … Part of what 'Star Trek' did well was use genre for storytelling, and that was what we wanted to explore in this series.”

He is, of course, absolutely correct; that is exactly what "Trek" has traditionally used genre episodes for. When "The Original Series" went to the Nazi planet, it was one of the first and earliest examples of directly confronting fascism and Nazism on American television. When the show played with Greek gods, it took the moment to have a groundbreaking interracial kiss. Even when it went broad comedy in “The Trouble with Tribbles,” it at least kept its characters consistent and its universe coherent.

For the most part, that practice continued throughout classic "Trek" and even into the modern era, with genre being used to aid storytelling, not overwhelm it.

Season 4 of "Strange New Worlds" does none of this. It isn’t using genre as elevation; it’s using it as a distraction: a shiny gloss over a collection of episodes too afraid to say anything that will get the series accused of being “woke” or progressive. Later in the interview, Goldman claims that they can’t please everyone, but that seems like exactly what they were trying to do this season-- resulting, of course, in pleasing no one.

This season is running scared from the current moment, and it’s doing so by hiding behind gimmicks. Any previous series of "Trek" (or any great science fiction) would be tackling subjects such as immigration, fascism, war, or any other societal issue that is overwhelming us right now, but "SNW" is doing none of that, instead presenting farcical genre fare

Fear exists for one purpose; to be conquered

It’s hard not to draw a direct line from this approach to the purchase of Paramount by Skydance last year and the company’s new leadership, who are more than cozy with President Donald Trump. There seems to be little other reason that a franchise and series that were being bashed for being “too woke” and overly progressive would veer so hard into gimmickry that barely hides the hollow shell this show has become.

Rewatching the first three seasons of "SNW" shows how hard a turn this series has taken since the re-election of Trump and the steady march of companies trying to kowtow to a government that wants to squash progressive ideology.

The show has gone from telling powerful stories for both its characters and society to a series of running gags that do little more than slap the Federation delta onto people’s chests so people think it's still "Star Trek".

It isn’t. This season of nothingness is exactly what you get when you ask "Trek" not to push boundaries, not to be hopeful, not to be bold, and not to progress forward. When a show founded on speaking out and saying something spends an entire season running away from doing just that, it’s not just a condemnation of the show itself; it’s a condemnation of the creative process behind it.

The real issue with this season isn’t the attempt to play in genre for ten episodes straight; it’s that the reason they did it was fear, not hope.

It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of "Star Trek" before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.

You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say.

That should trouble any Trekkie. "Star Trek" — a show built on progressive ideals, thoughtful characters, and boundary-breaking television — was completely and totally afraid to say anything at all.

Mash it up, Scotty

To be clear, "Star Trek" is no stranger to genre mashups, and they're not inherently a bad thing. Trek has been running for nearly 1,000 total episodes, and they've been doing mashups since the very first season of "Star Trek: The Original Series", which featured gangster, historical fiction, and war-themed episodes.

The holodeck took things further, giving the writers an excuse to set the action anywhere they could dream up. No more alien planets that look suspiciously like Earth were necessary to completely flip the series’ genre; just work up a hologram malfunction and suddenly "Trek" is a Sherlock Holmes-esque mystery or a noir thriller. And even without the holodeck, genres are fluid things that often take from each other to tell stories within each other’s realms.

But while "Trek" has always dabbled, it's never done an entire season of genre episodes… in fact, that might be unprecedented in all of science fiction TV itself, let alone "Star Trek". This season of "SNW" didn’t use occasional gimmicks to take a break from space fare; it was all gimmick, all the time.

Check out the episode rundown below:

  • Episode 1: Dinosaur adventure/western (Land of the Lost)
  • Episode 2: Space horror (Event Horizon)
  • Episode 3: Raunchy comedy (The Hangover)
  • Episode 4: Wartime drama (Casablanca)*
  • Episode 5: Puppets (The Muppets)
  • Episode 6: Disaster movie/real-time story (The Poseidon Adventure)
  • Episode 7: Soap opera (Days of Our Lives)
  • Episode 8: Cold War film/submarine movie (The Hunt for Red October)
  • Episode 9: Fairytale fantasy (Anything with a dragon)
  • Episode 10: Star Trek (Yes, this episode was basically SNW mashing up with TOS, and we're counting that).

* Some of you are screaming that Episode 4 was a noir. It was not. Not everything in black and white with fedoras is noir.

"Strange New Worlds" season 4 was genre-blending at scale. This wasn’t a hint of another genre influencing the episode; it was full-blown immersion into each and every one.

In the past, when other genres have come into "Trek", the series still felt tonally consistent; the characters never bent to the will of the genre, and its direction stayed the same. There were multiple episodes this season that felt nothing like a "Star Trek" episode.

Season 4 of "Strange New Worlds" does none of this. It isn’t using genre as elevation; it’s using it as a distraction: a shiny gloss over a collection of episodes too afraid to say anything that will get the series accused of being “woke” or progressive. Later in the interview, Goldman claims that they can’t please everyone, but that seems like exactly what they were trying to do this season-- resulting, of course, in pleasing no one.

This season is running scared from the current moment, and it’s doing so by hiding behind gimmicks. Any previous series of "Trek" (or any great science fiction) would be tackling subjects such as immigration, fascism, war, or any other societal issue that is overwhelming us right now, but "SNW" is doing none of that, instead presenting farcical genre fare

There seems to be little other reason that a franchise and series that were being bashed for being “too woke” and overly progressive would veer so hard into gimmickry that barely hides the hollow shell this show has become.

Rewatching the first three seasons of "SNW" shows how hard a turn this series has taken since the re-election of Trump and the steady march of companies trying to kowtow to a government that wants to squash progressive ideology.

The show has gone from telling powerful stories for both its characters and society to a series of running gags that do little more than slap the Federation delta onto people’s chests so people think it's still "Star Trek".

It isn’t. This season of nothingness is exactly what you get when you ask "Trek" not to push boundaries, not to be hopeful, not to be bold, and not to progress forward. When a show founded on speaking out and saying something spends an entire season running away from doing just that, it’s not just a condemnation of the show itself; it’s a condemnation of the creative process behind it.

The real issue with this season isn’t the attempt to play in genre for ten episodes straight; it’s that the reason they did it was fear, not hope.

]]> <![CDATA[ Medusa's eye, Halloween fireballs and more: 5 skywatching targets to look out for this spooky season ]]> The spooky season is officially here! To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies.

Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects.

Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites.

The Pleiades open star cluster

Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore. Ancient Celtic druids would hold the celebration of Samhain — the precursor to Halloween — when the star cluster reached its highest point in the autumn night sky at midnight.

The veil separating the worlds of the living and the dead was believed to be at its thinnest around this time, granting the departed a brief window to visit the living before the realms separated once again.

The Pleiades appears as a tight collection of six or seven bright twinkling stars to the naked eye, while a pair of binoculars will reveal dozens more of the 1,000-strong star cluster.

Stargazers in the U.S. can find the Pleiades using the three familiar stars of Orion's Belt, which glisten in the eastern sky in the hours preceding midnight. Trace an imaginary line upward through the trio of stars until you find the bright orange star Aldebaran, which represents an eye of the great bull represented in the constellation Taurus. The Pleiades can be found glowing less than 15 degrees above! (Reminder: Your clenched fist held at arm's length covers about 10 degrees of sky.)

The 'Demon Star' Algol

Next we turn our gaze to the "Demon Star" Algol — a beautiful binary system that represents an eye of the monstrous Gorgon Medusa, whose severed head is depicted in the constellation Perseus.

The demonic eye appears to "wink" at us every 2.867 days, as one of a pair of co-orbiting stars eclipses the other, making Algol appear 3.3 times dimmer than usual at the climax, or "minima," of each 10-hour eclipse. Algol won't be eclipsed on Halloween night in 2026, though you may notice its light dim during the surrounding minima on Oct. 29 and Nov. 1, according to Sky and Telescope.

Cetus, the sea monster

The night sky is often described as a sea of stars, so it's only fitting that a monster lurks within its depths. The constellation Cetus — also known as the sea monster, or the whale — can be found shining in the southeastern sky after sunset in late October, with the circlet of stars representing the monster's head glistening to the right of the Pleiades for viewers in the U.S.

In Greek mythology, Cetus was a mighty sea beast that terrorized the coast of Aethiopia under the command of the god Poseidon, according to the website for NASA's Chandra X-Ray Observatory. The sea beast was eventually killed by the hero Perseus, who in some tellings used the severed head of medusa to turn Cetus to stone!

Spiderwebs on the moon

Look to the lunar disk in the week surrounding the full moon on Oct. 26 and you may notice a bright network of spiderweb-like patterns surrounding the Tycho, Copernicus and Kepler craters.

Thankfully, these aren't the nests of some colossal moon-dwelling arachnids, but streaks of bright material cast across the lunar surface by the violent impacts that created the bright young craters. They're best viewed around the full moon phase, when the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky.

Halloween fireballs

Our last pick is going to take a great deal of patience, and a good amount of luck! Look out for bright, slow-moving meteors belonging to the Taurid meteor shower, which appear to streak away from a patch of sky close to the Pleiades in the constellation Taurus (hence the name).

The Taurids are comprised of two separate meteor showers — the Northern Taurids and Southern Taurids — which are active in late October as Earth passes through the debris trails left by the 3-mile-wide (4.8 kilometers) Comet 2P/Encke.

Taurids are known for producing bright "fireball" meteors, which are often called "Halloween fireballs" because they tend to coincide with the annual celebration. They're spectacular and can appear anytime after the constellation Taurus rises above the horizon, which is shortly after sunset in October for stargazers in the U.S.. But they're also very rare, so it's best to treat the fireballs as a bonus if you're lucky enough to spot one, rather than a target to plan your nights around, at least outside of the shower's peaks in early November.

Be sure to check out our beginners tips for skywatching if you're a newcomer to exploring the night sky, along with our picks of the best binoculars and telescope deals that'll have you exploring everything from the moon and stars to impressive deep sky objects in no time.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (video) ]]>

SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast.

The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California).

The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes.

The booster, meanwhile, reoriented for its descent back to Earth. As the mission clock passed 8 minutes, B1063 began its landing burn, and it touched down about 20 seconds later on SpaceX's droneship "Of Course I Still Love You." This was the 36th launch and landing for B1063, which notably launched NASA's DART asteroid-smashing mission in November 2021.

The Falcon 9's upper stage completed its first engine burn shortly after B1063 landed and will coast for about 45 minutes before initiating a second and final orbital insertion burn. Following that burn's execution, deployment of the vehicle's 27 satellites into LEO is scheduled to begin 62 minutes after launch.

Previous Booster B1063 launches

Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich | DART | Transporter-7 | Iridium OneWeb | SDA-0B | NROL-113 | NROL-167 | NROL-149 | NAOS | 26 Starlink missions

Today's Starlink liftoff adds to SpaceX's growing constellation of more than 11,000 active spacecraft. But Starlinks aren't launching quite as often as they used to, as SpaceX shifts its focus from the Falcon 9 to its bigger and more powerful Starship rocket.

Starship is designed for full reusability and is equipped with a payload bay outfitted to accommodate SpaceX's upgraded Version 3 Starlink satellites, which are too large for the workhorse Falcon 9. Starship is still under development, but once the rocket begins operational flights (and that day is getting closer), SpaceX plans to phase out the Falcon 9 and its Falcon Heavy variant almost entirely.

Falcon 9's 100th launch of 2026 was the Starlink 10-49 group from SpaceX's pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, which was later revealed to be the final Falcon 9 Starlink mission that would fly from Florida's Space Coast. The same might soon be true for Starlink launches from the West Coast as well.

The reduction in missions lifting off from Florida has slowed Falcon 9's Starlink launch cadence considerably. At their peak, these missions were flying every two to three days. But the most recent one before today lifted off 11 days ago, and that launch itself was the first Starlink mission in more than three weeks.

Today's launch was the 116th Falcon 9 flight so far in 2026, with about three-quarters of those being dedicated to Starlink. The reduced cadence will likely solidify 2025 as the Falcon 9's busiest year ever, with 165 launches completed. At its current rate, the Falcon 9 is expected to fly just under 150 missions by the end of this year.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA lays out plan for Artemis 3 moon-lander test flight —but when will it launch? ]]> NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight.

The agency laid out a detailed concept of operations for Artemis III today (Oct. 23) during a press conference at Kennedy Space Center, stressing how important the flight is to its moon plans and how challenging it will be to make everything go right.

"We're launching three of the most powerful rockets in the world, and undertaking what is likely the most complicated launch campaign ever undertaken," Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, said during today's event, which lasted more than two hours.

Those three rockets are NASA's Space Launch System (SLS), SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's New Glenn, all of which will fly from Florida's Space Coast.

If all goes according to plan, New Glenn will lift off first, carrying Blue Origin's Blue Moon lunar lander to low Earth orbit (LEO). SLS will go next, launching the Artemis III astronauts — NASA's Randy Bresnik, Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio, and the European Space Agency's Luca Parmitano — aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft.

SLS will deploy Orion into a highly elliptical orbit, one that gets as close to Earth as 18 miles (29 kilometers) and as far away as 1,122 miles (1,806 km), according to Parsons. The capsule will then maneuver itself into an orbit with an altitude of about 345 miles (555 km).

"That's really about getting thermal stability," Parsons said. "Orion was built as a deep-space vehicle, and so we're going to have to really manage the thermal environments, which are higher in a low Earth orbit."

The Artemis III crew will spend two days checking out Orion and its systems in LEO before meeting up with Blue Moon, which will take place on Flight Day 3 at an altitude of 273 miles (439 km).

"Over the next two days, the crew will conduct operations docked with Blue Moon," Parsons said. "They're going to open up the hatch. They're going to enter the lander. They're going to evaluate the environmental controls, the life support systems. We'll confirm that the spacecraft can maintain the right atmospheric pressure, and we're also going to test emergency scenarios, dual vehicle control, and we're going to put our Mission Control teams through their paces."

After those operations are complete — likely on Flight Day 6 or thereabouts — Starship will launch, with a specially built docking adapter on its nose.

The SpaceX vehicle — the 171-foot-tall (52 meters) upper stage of its fully reusable Starship megarocket — will meet up with Orion in LEO on Flight Day 8, at an altitude of about 237 miles (381 km). But this will be a very different encounter than the rendezvous with Blue Moon.

"The demonstration with Starship is shorter, about two hours," Parsons said. "The crew will not enter the Starship during the mission, but it gives us critical data and allows us to really understand the forces of docking, how we're going to push, how we're going to work together."

Artemis III will continue for another six to nine days after Orion undocks from Starship before finally heading back down to Earth for a parachute-aided ocean splashdown. (The nominal mission length is 14 days, Parsons said, but it could last as long as 17 days.)

During that time, the crew will evaluate their survival suits — something that didn't get done during the 10-day Artemis II flight around the moon this past April — and do a variety of other work as well, from detailed health assessments to scientific experiments and technology demonstrations. The main goal is to keep everything on track for Artemis IV, which will land astronauts near the moon's south pole in 2028, if all goes to plan.

"Everything we do on Artemis III is designed to reduce risk for our future lunar landing missions," Parsons said. "We're teaching these teams how to work together, how to make critical real-time mission decisions, all in an environment that is low Earth orbit, where if something goes wrong, we can come home much more quickly."

It's unclear at the moment which of these two privately developed landers — Blue Moon or Starship — will fly on Artemis IV, pulling off the first crewed lunar touchdown since Apollo 17 in 1972.

NASA is still preserving optionality, "to give both of our lunar landing partners the greatest opportunity for readiness in advance of astronauts landing on the moon in 2028," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said during today's event.

"We have no intention of surrendering a viable path to the surface before the data and schedule compels us to do so," he added.

No matter what decision NASA makes for Artemis IV, both Blue Moon and Starship should hit the gray dirt relatively soon, according to Parsons. "Regardless of who goes first, both providers are planning for lunar landing missions in 2028," he said.

And those missions will be quite different from each other. For example, on Blue Origin touchdowns, Orion will meet up with Blue Moon in lunar orbit. On SpaceX landings, however, Starship will likely dock with the NASA capsule in Earth orbit and propel it to the moon, Parsons said — the "push" he referred to above.

It remains unclear when exactly Artemis III will launch. NASA is targeting the summer of next year but may find it tough to meet that timeline: Last month, in an internal memo, Isaacman told agency employees that Artemis III was about 90 days behind schedule.

Some of the biggest challenges have involved the supply chain for the mission's lunar landers, Parsons said during today's event. But he and Isaacman both stressed that NASA is confident in its ability to work through such issues.

"We're moving with real speed and purpose right now," Isaacman said.

The SpaceX vehicle — the 171-foot-tall (52 meters) upper stage of its fully reusable Starship megarocket — will meet up with Orion in LEO on Flight Day 8, at an altitude of about 237 miles (381 km). But this will be a very different encounter than the rendezvous with Blue Moon.

"The demonstration with Starship is shorter, about two hours," Parsons said. "The crew will not enter the Starship during the mission, but it gives us critical data and allows us to really understand the forces of docking, how we're going to push, how we're going to work together."

Artemis III will continue for another six to nine days after Orion undocks from Starship before finally heading back down to Earth for a parachute-aided ocean splashdown. (The nominal mission length is 14 days, Parsons said, but it could last as long as 17 days.)

During that time, the crew will evaluate their survival suits — something that didn't get done during the 10-day Artemis II flight around the moon this past April — and do a variety of other work as well, from detailed health assessments to scientific experiments and technology demonstrations. The main goal is to keep everything on track for Artemis IV, which will land astronauts near the moon's south pole in 2028, if all goes to plan.

"Everything we do on Artemis III is designed to reduce risk for our future lunar landing missions," Parsons said. "We're teaching these teams how to work together, how to make critical real-time mission decisions, all in an environment that is low Earth orbit, where if something goes wrong, we can come home much more quickly."

It's unclear at the moment which of these two privately developed landers — Blue Moon or Starship — will fly on Artemis IV, pulling off the first crewed lunar touchdown since Apollo 17 in 1972.

NASA is still preserving optionality, "to give both of our lunar landing partners the greatest opportunity for readiness in advance of astronauts landing on the moon in 2028," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said during today's event.

"We have no intention of surrendering a viable path to the surface before the data and schedule compels us to do so," he added.

No matter what decision NASA makes for Artemis IV, both Blue Moon and Starship should hit the gray dirt relatively soon, according to Parsons. "Regardless of who goes first, both providers are planning for lunar landing missions in 2028," he said.

And those missions will be quite different from each other. For example, on Blue Origin touchdowns, Orion will meet up with Blue Moon in lunar orbit. On SpaceX landings, however, Starship will likely dock with the NASA capsule in Earth orbit and propel it to the moon, Parsons said — the "push" he referred to above.

It remains unclear when exactly Artemis III will launch. NASA is targeting the summer of next year but may find it tough to meet that timeline: Last month, in an internal memo, Isaacman told agency employees that Artemis III was about 90 days behind schedule.

Some of the biggest challenges have involved the supply chain for the mission's lunar landers, Parsons said during today's event. But he and Isaacman both stressed that NASA is confident in its ability to work through such issues.

"We're moving with real speed and purpose right now," Isaacman said.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission ]]>

On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station.

The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts.

Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station, they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node.

After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module. This made room for Harmony to then dock at its permanent home next to the Destiny module.

Why it mattered

In 2007, the International Space Station was much smaller than it is today in terms of living space for its astronaut crew. The Harmony connecting module changed all that.

The STS-120 mission opened a new phase of ISS expansion by adding a vital connecting hub for future modules. Prior to Harmony's launch, the last new room addition to the ISS had occurred in 2001, when Russia's Pirs docking module (since discarded) arrived.

The Harmony module (its original name was Node 2), was the second NASA-led hub module (after the Unity, or Node 1, module) for the ISS. It was built for NASA by the Italy-based Thales Alenia Space and is covered with five "common berthing mechanisms," or connecting points for different ISS modules.

After the two-week STS-120 flight, Harmony was moved from a temporary berth at the Unity module to the forward port on the NASA's main Destiny laboratory. Once there, it served as a connection point for Europe's Columbus lab on the starboard side, and Japan's massive Kibo lab on the port side. Some of its ports have been used by visiting caargo ships and a docking port on its roof allows visiting vehicles to park there.

Inside the module are eight payload racks that include four used for avionics and four others for either stowage or crew quarters. NASA's astronaut crew quarters are based in the Harmony module. The name Harmony was selected durng a public naming contest by NASA.

]]> <![CDATA[ Halley's Comet dazzles from afar in spectacular astrophoto of Orionid meteor shower ]]>

Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity.

Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth, but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky.

McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21. Each of the shooting stars can be seen racing away from the shower's apparent point of origin — or radiant — which is located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion.

Successfully imaging a shooting star takes a combination of skill, luck and patience. McCollum photographed the meteors over the course of multiple 30-second exposures taken with a Canon EOS Ra camera and RF 28-70 f2.0 lens, which was fixed unerringly on the radiant with the aid of a star tracker. The individual exposures were then combined into a single composite image using the astrophoto software PixInsight.

Canon EOS R7 camera

The Canon EOS R7 is the best camera for beginners. Despite its crop sensor, the EOS R7 can rival most full-frame cameras. It features a 34.4MP sensor, ISO range up to 32,000 and a video capability of 4K UHD 60p. It has the best tools to help a beginner master photography. Read our full Canon EOS R7 review.

The familiar stars of Orion's Belt glisten to the right of McCollum's image, close to the glow of the Orion Nebula — one of the nearest major star forming regions to Earth. The Rosette Nebula (Caldwell 49) can also be spotted embedded in the dense starfield and dust lanes of the Milky Way's galactic plane, which runs diagonally through the composite image, as can numerous star clusters.

The Orionid meteor shower is active until Nov. 7, so be sure to head outside over the next few nights for a chance to spot one of Comet 1P/Halley's dazzling shooting stars. If you're lucky, you may even spot a Halloween Fireball belonging to the Taurid meteor shower, as Earth passes through the debris streams cast off by Comet 2P/Encke!

Why not read our handy guide to photographing shooting stars? You can also take a look at our picks of the best lenses and cameras for astrophotography available in 2026, including the Canon EOS R8, which delivers the essential interval shooting functionality you need to capture meteors without bursting the bank.

]]> <![CDATA[ Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo? ]]> Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War.

Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise.

Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.

This year’s full remake of Combat Evolved's campaign delivered exactly what it promised: a shiny, 2026 version of the game that made audiences fall in love with the franchise. It was a clear attempt to reignite faith in 343’s vision, but how is a faithful, shinier remake proof of anything?

It might not even matter anymore, as the new Xbox leadership has rocked the ship again, leaving Master Chief and the universe’s future cloudier than ever before. Now, with rumors of a reboot being considered at new steward Activision, is there hope for the Spartans, or will Xbox run into another dead end?

Rebooted or not, Halo needs to leave Master Chief behind

It looks like the ‘Halo Studios’ moniker only lasted a single (remade) game, as Xbox has recently announced that Call of Duty maker and publisher Activision — which houses many FPS-oriented studios — is taking over development, essentially leaving the 343 veterans as a minor support studio, which translates into more layoffs.

If we put aside the human and institutional cost of this whole back-and-forth over the years (a big ask in today’s climate), there are reasons to be optimistic about the quality of an Activision-developed Halo. Regardless of what you think about the Call of Duty IP in 2026 and the publisher’s overall vision for it, it’s clear there’s plenty of talent holding everything together and, more importantly, enough experience to iterate on what Halo’s multiplayer side needs to shine bright again.

But this won’t fix the larger issue with Halo, which is that Master Chief should’ve been left behind long ago. Like it or not, it’s difficult to deny Halo’s “golden era” ended with Halo: Reach (Bungie’s swansong under Xbox) and the Halo Wars spinoffs, which took the series into the real-time strategy genre. These games were wildly different, but they had one core thing in common: they made the sci-fi setting feel bigger instead of smaller, offering the perfect blueprint to build upon in a post-Halo 3 world.

There’s nothing inherently wrong with the Master Chief. Franchises can be built around iconic characters like Mario or Lara Croft. But in the post-Bungie era, his role changed from an extremely competent Spartan soldier to a space messiah. Halo 4, 5, and Infinite used sci-fi nonsense to transform him into this larger-than-life figure, rendering the rest of the UNSC largely powerless in the process.

It’s the same mistake ID Software made with Doomguy, centering the story on how super special he is, and not on the world he inhabits. Now rumours are rumbling that Activision’s reboot might focus on Chief’s origins; that's the last thing Halo needs.

Are Halo 2 and 3 remakes happening?

Forgetting Activision’s next Halo for a second, we were teased with (even if there wasn’t an official confirmation from Xbox) at least a Halo 2 remake via Halo: Campaign Evolved’s alternative ending.

Back in May 2026, renowned insider Rebs Gaming confidently reported that Halo 2 and 3 remakes were in development. But can fans realistically expect them after new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s latest shakeup?

Halo Studios could have done a "fine" job with safe remakes of the two original Halo sequels while Activision handles new projects. It’s hard to reject that approach, especially after Xbox finding success with Bethesda’s The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered and confirming two Fallout remasters are in the works. It seems like money waiting to be made, but the remakes could be cooked too.

Xbox and 343/Halo Studios have made plenty of mistakes with Halo, but the killer has always been their lack of conviction in their ideas. And look, nostalgia shouldn’t be the driving force behind a franchise in dire need of reinvention, but I’m far more annoyed by the creative rollbacks, flip-flopping, and now the loss of knowledge and talent accompanying the gutting of Halo Studios.

Xbox Live Action

We haven’t even touched on the mess that was the live-action Halo show. It lasted only two seasons, had John-117 walking around outside the Mjolnir armor for most of its runtime, and was cancelled just as the story finally got to the titular Halo. Why would you stray so far from the source material, and how do you miss the mark so badly?

In many ways, it perfectly encapsulated what’s been wrong with Halo as a whole for so many years. The powers that be can’t decide what they really want from it, and thus it’s stuck, unable to leave the past behind or convincingly establish a new horizon for itself. Other franchises have run into the same issues — looking at you, Star Wars — but Halo has been stuck in this purgatory for 15+ years, as Xbox leaders and strategy shifts come and go.

Could Xbox’s newly-formed XP division deliver the focused big-screen adaptation the series has always deserved? I’m sure that’s the plan, but even a cursory glance back at Xbox’s handling of the franchise for the past decade or so says no.

Halo’s deep problems won’t be fixed overnight, and throwing a bunch of hard-working developers to the curb certainly won’t help. Halo’s current struggles didn’t come from Halo Studios or 343 Industries; they came from impatient and incompetent leadership calling the property-defining shots. I’ve seen nothing to suggest that’s changed.

]]> <![CDATA[ Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026 ]]>

The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year.

What is it?

At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. The spacecraft was put through environmental testing that explored how the vehicle will fare in the extreme conditions it will experience on its ride to the surface of the moon.

This testing simulated the extreme temperatures, shaking and even the sounds that the spacecraft will experience from launch to landing. And, as JPL announced recently, the lander passed this series of tests with flying colors, as we can see in this image snapped Aug. 31 of the lander inside the 25-foot-wide (7.6 meters) space simulator at JPL.

"NASA JPL’s Environmental Test Laboratory has been putting robotic explorers to the test since the Ranger program gave us NASA’s first up-close views of the moon's surface in the mid-1960s. We’re proud to provide our expertise and facilities to support this new phase of commercial lunar exploration," Charles Whetsel, manager for the Exploration Systems Development Office at JPL, said in a statement.

Why is it incredible?

Griffin-1 is expected to launch to the moon later this year as part of NASA's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative. The spacecraft will carry over 1,100 pounds (455 kilograms) of cargo to its landing site near the lunar south pole.

In this cargo will be science experiments and new technologies that will be tested on the moon's surface, including Astrolab's FLIP rover, which will explore the lunar surface with a history-making supercomputer onboard.

This suite of experimental hardware won't just expand our understanding of the moon up close. Griffin-1's exploration will also help set the stage for a future, crewed moon base, which NASA aims to build near the south pole over the next half-decade or so.

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/tezba-dreva-v-chlumci-mela-ponicit-zastaveni-krizove-cesty-poskozena-je-i-stezka_2610241336_mkm</link>
 <description>Jedno ze 14 zastavení křížové cesty v Chlumci na Ústecku poničil podle radnice státní podnik Lesy ČR (LČR) při těžbě dřeva. Na místě zůstaly i vylámané obrubníky na obecní cestě. Starostka města Veronika Srnková (Šance pro Chlumec) žádá nápravu, protože cestu na vrchol Horky lidé hodně využívají.
</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-114588128_261024-133843_mkm_0.jpg?itok=ju25ULFF" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 16:36:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Rozhodnout den předem, že se bude hlasovat nad ránem, je bizarní, říká politolog k hlasování o poplatcích</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/hlasovani-ruseni-poplatky-za-rozhlas-a-televizi-politolog_2610241611_tec</link>
 <description>„Politická kultura zaplakala,“ říká v rozhovoru pro Radiožurnál k pátečnímu dění ohledně hlasování o rušení koncesionářských poplatků pro veřejnoprávní média politolog z Filozofické fakulty Západočeské univerzity v Plzni Přemysl Rosůlek. Přesto podle něj může být tento „bizarní“ postup do jisté míry legitimní. „Zejména poté, co došlo k novele jednacího řádu, před kterou se nebylo možné shodnout ani na tom, jaký bude program.“</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/a_zuj1198_260930-072440_mda.jpg?itok=uEG87QjF" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 16:11:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Bezprecedentní zásah proti občanské společnosti.‘ Piráti navrhnou odvolání Okamury z čela Sněmovny</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/tomio-okamura-odvolani-z-cela-snemovny-pirati-hrib_2610241534_tec</link>
 <description>Opoziční Piráti navrhnou na nejbližším jednání Sněmovny odvolání jejího předsedy Tomia Okamury (SPD). Na síti X to v sobotu uvedl předseda strany Zdeněk Hřib. Při pátečním a sobotním jednání o návrhu na zrušení televizních a rozhlasových poplatků Okamura podle Pirátů bezprecedentně zasáhl proti občanské společnosti omezováním přístupu na jednání Sněmovny. Okamura uvedl, že na „neustálé lži, útoky a výkřiky“ nebude reagovat.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/a_zuj1218_260930-072442_mda.jpg?itok=mUoiNCU4" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 15:34:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Financování ČT a ČRo bude jako mandatorní výdaj, řekl Babiš. Protesty srovnal s útokem na Kapitol</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/babis-zadne-ohrozeni-demokracie-financovani-ct-a-cro-bude-jako-mandatorni-vydaj_2610241527_jho</link>
 <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) v sobotu na sociálních sítích řekl, že financování České televize a Českého rozhlasu po zrušení poplatků zaručí zákon jako mandatorní výdaj a bude navázáno na inflaci. Obě média podle něj získají větší jistotu, stabilitu a nezávislost. Prohlásil to po celonočním jednání Sněmovny, která přes odpor opozice návrh novely poslala do druhého čtení. Babiš také opět vyzval opozici, aby přestala eskalovat situaci ve společnosti.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/dsc_7537_260925-232202_jgr.jpg?itok=ugU5o31H" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 15:27:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Za protektorátu tajně vydávali časopis, příběh židovských studentů teď vypráví virtuální realita</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/virtualni-realita-priblizuje-holokaust-studentum-ceske-budejovice_2610241526_zfr</link>
 <description>Za protektorátu tajně tvořili časopis plný povídek, básní, koláží i humoru. Příběh dospívajících Židů z Českých Budějovic a jejich časopisu Klepy teď přibližuje nová aplikace ve virtuální realitě. Paměť národa Jižní Čechy ji zasadila do prostředí Kendeho vily.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2ed49cd16f8717fdbf93_261024-121218_zfr.jpg?itok=SPoxnsxc" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 15:26:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Žádám, aby politici utišili emoce, vyzval Pavel. Způsob jednání o poplatcích podle něj budí pochybnosti</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/zadam-aby-politici-utisili-emoce-vyzval-pavel-zpusob-jednani-o-poplatcich-podle_2610241454_jho</link>
 <description>Neočekávané zařazení a noční víkendové hlasování o návrhu novely zákona, jež ruší poplatky pro Českou televizi (ČT) a Český rozhlas (ČRo), podkopává víru v dobré úmysly a vede k vážným pochybnostem o záměrech předkladatelů. Na síti X to v sobotu uvedl prezident Petr Pavel. Doplnil, že média veřejné služby řadí mezi základní pilíře české demokracie a každé velké změně má předcházet široká odborná i veřejná diskuse.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/zuj_2293_251006-131214_zuj.jpg?itok=lMnj6pR3" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 14:54:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>OTÁZKY A ODPOVĚDI: Co znamená schválení návrhu o koncesionářských poplatcích? A co bude dál?</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/otazky-a-odpovedi-co-znamena-schvaleni-navrhu-o-koncesionarskych-poplatcich-a-co_2610241447_pik</link>
 <description>Poslanci v sobotu ráno podpořili v prvním čtení vládní návrh o změně financování České televize a Českého rozhlasu. Podle novely by už média nefungovala na základě plateb koncesionářských poplatků, ale byla by financovaná přímo ze státního rozpočtu. Co aktuálně prohlasovaný návrh znamená? Byl průběh jednání o tomto bodu obvyklý? A co teď bude následovat? Web iROZHLAS.cz přináší odpovědi.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/zuj_0695_250603-160714_zuj.jpg?itok=250cDtvc" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 14:47:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>

  <item>
   <title>Dušičky se letos prodraží. Přesto lze s letákovými slevami ušetřit</title>

   <description>Oproti minulému roku v obchodech podražily svíčky i umělé květinové vazby. Díky akčním letákům ale mohou zákazníci ušetřit za dušičkový sortiment v průměru o 13 procent. Vyplývá to z analýzy společnosti Česká distribuční.</description>

    <media:description>Dušičková výzdoba může zůstat krásná i po dešti, větru a prvních mrazících. Stačí zvolit odolné rostliny, přírodní materiály a dekorace, které na hrobě dobře drží.</media:description>

  <item>
   <title>Konec poplatků za ČT a rozhlas: Co bude následovat, kdy je lidé přestanou platit</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/konec-poplatku-za-ct-a-rozhlas-co-bude-nasledovat-kdy-je-lide-prestanou-platit/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Poslanci po bouřlivém nočním jednání z pátku na sobotu schválili v prvním čtení vládní návrh na zrušení koncesionářských poplatků za Českou televizi a Český rozhlas. Financování veřejnoprávních médií má nově převzít státní rozpočet. Deník.cz se v otázkách a odpovědích podíval na to, kdy domácnosti reálně mohou přestat platit poplatky. Návrh totiž má před sebou ještě dlouhou legislativní cestu, kterou podle všeho doprovodí tvrdé opoziční obstrukce, protesty v ulicích i ohlášené stávky dotčených médií veřejné služby.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Po změně času hrozí cyklistům i chodcům další pokuty. Neznají pravidla</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/doprava/zmena-casu-nova-pravidla-pro-cyklisty-i-chodce-hrozi-pokuty/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=doprava</link>
   <description>V noci ze soboty 24. října na neděli 25. října se Česko vrátí k zimnímu času. Slunce tak bude zapadat o hodinu dříve, na ručičkách hodinek už před pátou odpoledne. Na silnicích se zhorší podmínky pro chodce, cyklisty i řidiče, kteří budou častěji cestovat za šera a tmy. Deník.cz se blíže podíval na povinnosti, na které upozorňuje policie. Odborníci na bezpečnost na silnicích přidávají rady, kdy reflexní prvky a funkční osvětlení zachraňují životy. Aktuální období totiž patří k nejrizikovějším v roce.</description>

    <media:description>Se změnou času přichází tma dřív. Pozor na povinnosti chodců a cyklistů. Nedodržením pravidel riskují životy i pokuty.</media:description>

  <item>
   <title>Dobrá duše Petra se stará o postiženého syna i bratra</title>
   <link>https://karlovarsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/dobra-duse-petra-se-stara-o-postizeneho-syna-i-bratra/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>„Prostě se musím postarat.“ V několika slovech je možná celý příběh čtyřicetileté Petry Traganové z Toužimska. Maminky, která se po těžké životní situaci ocitla v roli člověka, na němž závisí péče o jejího syna Tomáše. Pomáhá i postiženému bratrovi. Nečeká se založenýma rukama a hledá možnosti, jak pomoci. Zkouší rehabilitace, učí syna používat elektrický vozík a raduje se z každého malého pokroku.</description>

   <title>Dětské kroužky raketově zdražily. Rodiče jsou zoufalí, obracejí se na sbírky</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/skolstvi-a-vzdelavani/cesko-skolstvi-krouzky-zdrazily-cena-kritika/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=skolstvi-a-vzdelavani</link>
   <description>Rodiče čelí ve školním roce 2026/2027 výraznému nárůstu výdajů za volnočasové kroužky. Podle statistik stouply příspěvky ve většině sportovních oddílů, přičemž výdaje rostou i za další aktivity. Stále častěji se proto rodiče obracejí s žádostmi o finanční výpomoc na sbírky a různé projekty, které jim s nouzí pomáhají. Týká se to především samoživitelů. Dobrou zprávou je, že solidarita u Čechů stoupá a přispívají v různých sbírkách.</description>
   <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 04:30:00 +0200</pubDate>

   <title>Jak si zajistit místo v domově důchodců? V předstihu do něj investovat</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/cesko-jak-si-zajistt-misto-v-domove-duchodcu-investovat-do-nej/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Na aktivní důchod si spoří asi dvě třetiny Čechů, na péči ve stáří jich má ale vyčleněné nějaké peníze jen zhruba čtvrtina. Vyplývá to z aktuálního průzkumu. Odborníci upozorňují, že společnost stárne a nějaký typ péče potřebuje asi polovina starších lidí. Nově si zájemci mohou investovat na garantované lůžko v domově seniorů.</description>

      <title>Všechny převezl a nafotil sopečné závěje na Kanárech. Málem ho pohřbily zaživa</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/slavne-fotografie-emilio-morenatti-sopka-la-palma-cumbre-vieja-popel-kyjev-pakistan.A261020_130835_zahranicni_aha#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Dystopická krajina pokrytá černým sněhem. Když před pěti lety vybuchla sopka Cumbre Vieja, celý svět obletěly snímky krajiny pohřbené pod nánosy popela. Pořídil je Emilio Morenatti, fotograf s bohatými zkušenostmi z válečných zón. O fíglech reportérské práce, únosu v Gaze či rehabilitaci po ztrátě levé nohy se rozpovídal pro seriál Slavné fotografie.</description>

<title>Vyzkoušeli jsme Muskův internet Starlink zdarma v letadle. Je to jako doma na gauči</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/vyzkouseli-jsme-muskuv-internet-starlink-zdarma-v-letadle-je-to-jako-doma-na-gauci/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Běžné komerční aerolinky postupně do své flotily nasazují internetové připojení Starlink od americké společnosti SpaceX Elona Muska. Vysokorychlostní satelitní internet se začíná objevovat i na evropských spojích. Lupa otestovala Starlink během letu z Prahy do Rigy v letadle loty&#353;ského přepravce airBaltic, který v tomto ohledu patří k průkopníkům a který přislíbil takto vybavit v&#353;echna svá letadla (pokud přežije současnou finanční krizi a vysoké zadlužení).</description>

<title>Státní financování ČT a rozhlasu se posouvá do druhého čtení. Hlasovalo se ve 4:36 ráno</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/statni-financovani-ct-a-rozhlasu-se-posouva-do-druheho-cteni-hlasovalo-se-ve-4-36-rano/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Vládní koalice v sobotu 24. října ve 4:36 ráno prosadila do druhého čtení návrh na zru&#353;ení televizních a rozhlasových poplatků. Financování obou médií má převzít stát. Způsob projednávání vyvolal kritiku mezinárodních organizací, představitelů vysokých &#353;kol i divadel a protesty před sněmovnou.</description>

<title>EU se snaží zmírnit nedávno zavedená obalová pravidla, která potápí malé e-shopy. Rada a Parlament se ale neshodnou, jak na to</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/eu-se-snazi-zmirnit-nedavno-zavedena-obalova-pravidla-ktera-potapi-male-e-shopy-rada-a-parlament-se-ale-neshodnou-jak-na-to/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Povinnost, která malým e-shopům komplikuje prodej do dal&#353;ích zemí EU, by se mohla pro malé e-shopy zmírnit. Evropský parlament i Rada EU chtějí pozastavit pravidlo, podle něhož musí firmy jmenovat zástupce pro roz&#353;ířenou odpovědnost výrobce v jednotlivých zemích, kam dodávají zboží v obalech. Neshodují se ale na tom, koho by se výjimka měla týkat.</description>

 <description>Americký vyjednavač Steve Witkoff opět navštívil Rusko. Tentokrát přivezl evropské a ukrajinské návrhy na ukončení války. Dosavadní americká diplomacie ale podle analytika Michala Smetany nenese žádné výsledky. „Je to spíše kontraproduktivní,“ upozorňuje pro Radiožurnál. Proč Donald Trump vychází vstříc Vladimiru Putinovi, zatímco na Ukrajinu vyvíjí stále větší tlak? A mohl by se evropským vyjednavačem s Kremlem stát český prezident Petr Pavel?</description>

<item>
 <title>Ve Francii protestovalo 800 000 lidí, z toho čtvrt milionu v Paříži. Vadí jim vysoké životní náklady</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/ve-francii-protestuje-800-000-lidi-z-toho-ctvrt-milionu-v-parizi-chteji-lepsi_2610241845_jho</link>
 <description>Ve Francii v sobotu protestovaly stovky tisíc lidí. Většinu doby byly protesty klidné, jen na závěr docházelo k násilnostem. Agentura AFP píše s odkazem na odbory o 800 000 protestujících, z toho čtvrt milionu v Paříži. Pařížská prefektura předtím informovala, že městem v sobotu prošel protestní průvod 110 000 lidí různých věkových skupin. Podobně jako jinde v zemi požadovali lepší veřejné služby a protestovali proti vysokým životním nákladům.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-24t150804z_5_261024-183333_jho.JPG?itok=6ba0Cn4P" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Francouzský soud uvalil vazbu na dvojici podezřelou ze založení požáru na radnici v Limoges</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/francouzsky-soud-uvalil-vazbu-na-dvojici-podezrelou-z-pozaru-radnice-v-limoges_2610241234_cen</link>
 <description>Francouzský soud uvalil vazbu na dvojici mužů, kteří jsou podezřelí z podílu na založení požáru radnice ve městě Limoges během demonstrace minulý víkend. Informovala o tom dnes agentura AFP. Dotyčným je 34 a 66 let, první z nich byl zadržen v úterý, druhý ve čtvrtek.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-18t151139z_7_261024-122847_cen.JPG?itok=bQ1aV8P_" type="image/jpeg" />

<item>
 <title>Severokorejský vůdce Kim Čong-un je na návštěvě Číny, do města u hranic KLDR přijel vlakem</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/severokorejsky-vudce-kim-cong-un-je-na-navsteve-ciny-do-mesta-u-hranic-kldr_2610241010_cen</link>
 <description>Severokorejský vůdce Kim Čong-un dorazil do čínského Tan-tungu na severokorejsko-čínské hranici. Informoval o tom Reuters s odvoláním na jihokorejskou agenturu Jonhap. V posledních dnech se spekulovalo o Kimově zdravotním stavu. Kim přicestoval vlakem po novém mostě přes hraniční řeku Ja-lu (korejsky Amnokkang) mezi severokorejským městem Sinuidžu a Tan-tungem. Ten přitom obě země otevřely teprve minulý týden, 12 let po jeho dokončení.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-23t222157z_8_261024-100344_cen.JPG?itok=9jsKA8EL" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Orlí hnízdo, někdejší Hitlerovo horské sídlo, které funguje jako horská restaurace, zachvátil požár</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/orli-hnizdo-nekdejsi-hitlerovo-horske-sidlo-ktere-funguje-jako-horska-restaurace_2610240920_cen</link>
 <description>Požár zachvátil v pátek večer Kehlsteinhaus, známý také jako Orlí hnízdo, někdejší horské sídlo nacistického vůdce Adolfa Hitlera v bavorských Alpách. Policie v sobotu oznámila, že v souvislosti s požárem zadržela podezřelého. Příčina požáru zatím není známa, napsala agentura DPA.</description>

<item>
 <title>Rusko a Ukrajina se dohodly na příměří v okupovaných Oleškách. Budou evakuováni civilisté</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-rusko-a-ukrajina-se-dohodly-na-primeri-v-okupovanych-oleskach-budou_2610240811_adn</link>
 <description>V Rusy okupovaném ukrajinském městě Olešky začne příští týden platit příměří. Má umožnit doručení humanitární pomoci a evakuaci civilního obyvatelstva. Oznámil to Bílý dům a potvrdily to Moskva i Kyjev. Rusové Olešky okupují od prvních dnů invaze v únoru 2022. Lidskoprávní organizace upozorňují, že místním chybí základní potraviny a jedí třeba i trávu.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-08t060037z_1_261024-080603_adn.JPG?itok=rICqRa5N" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Studentská opozice vyráží do boje proti Vučićovi. Co čekat od předčasných parlamentních voleb v Srbsku</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/srbsko-volby-studenti-vucic_2610240700_ula</link>
 <description>V Srbsku se budou v neděli konat předčasné parlamentní volby. Dnes už bývalý prezident Aleksandar Vučić je vyhlásil na začátku září. O pár týdnů později k nim přidal i svou rezignaci. Jeho hlavním soupeřem ale letos není opozice parlamentní, nýbrž ta studentská. Podle průzkumů jsou šance vyrovnané. Studenty k volbám dovedly už téměř dva roky trvající protivládní protesty, které zahájili po tragédii na vlakovém nádraží v Novém Sadu.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-19t100028z_7_261020-230423_ula.JPG?itok=qkgBa6JF" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 07:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Podlézat Putinovi jako Trump není namístě, vadí TOP 09. Pozlátko má v Rusku velkou roli, míní v ANO</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/podlezat-putinovi-jako-trump-neni-na-miste-vadi-top-09-pozlatko-ma-v-rusku_2610232337_jho</link>
 <description>Rusko tento týden znovu vyslalo rakety na Kyjev. Nedlouho předtím přitom dalo najevo, že v zásadě souhlasí s obnovením mírových rozhovorů. Na čí straně stojí Spojené státy? A co má dělat Evropa? „Jsem kritický na všechny strany, vidím i pokrytectví Evropské unie,“ upozorňuje europoslanec Tomáš Kubín (ANO). „Evropská diplomacie je paralyzovaná lidmi, jako je Andrej Babiš (ANO),“ kritizuje pro Český rozhlas Plus europoslanec Ondřej Kolář (TOP 09).</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/0e0b6feda40e0f333696ecadfb51a95c.png?itok=mYoy50Ki" type="image/png" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 23:37:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Mareček: Obvinění Kushnera stojí na anonymních zdrojích. Zapadá to ale do chování americké vlády</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/marecek-obvineni-kushnera-stoji-na-anonymnich-zdrojich-zapada-ale-do-chovani_2610231753_vsn</link>
 <description>Jared Kushner, zeť a velvyslanec Donalda Trumpa, popřel obvinění Vanity Fair, podle něhož nizozemská zpravodajská služba při sledování aktivit na jeho telefonu odhalila finanční transakce, do kterých byly zapojeny vlády z Blízkého východu. „Nevíme, do jaké míry hraje roli zájem USA a kdy záměr Trumpovy rodiny,“ říká pro Radiožurnál David Mareček, amerikanista z Katedry mezinárodních vztahů a evropských studií Metropolitní univerzity Praha.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-09-05t165914z_1_260906-062554_ape.JPG?itok=jHtCIgd3" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 17:53:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Netanjahu po útoku u Hebronu zvažuje největší operaci na Západním břehu od roku 1967</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/netanjahu-po-utoku-u-hebronu-zvazuje-nejvetsi-operaci-na-zapadnim-brehu-od-roku_2610231442_vsn</link>
 <description>Izraelský premiér Benjamin Netanjahu v pátek po střelbě u Hebronu prohlásil, že zvažuje na Západním břehu Jordánu největší vojenskou operaci od roku 1967. Napsala to izraelská média a agentura AFP. Podle Netanjahua je armáda připravena příkazy vykonat. Oznámení přichází několik dní před parlamentními volbami, v nichž bude šéf izraelského kabinetu usilovat o znovuzvolení.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/69580b50e98f3ff1a01622008e84f266.jpg?itok=ji63_dbo" type="image/jpeg" />

<description>Běžné komerční aerolinky postupně do své flotily nasazují internetové připojení Starlink od americké společnosti SpaceX Elona Muska. Lupa otestovala Starlink během letu z Prahy do Rigy v letadle loty&#353;ského přepravce airBaltic, který v tomto ohledu patří k průkopníkům a který přislíbil takto vybavit v&#353;echna svá letadla (pokud přežije současnou finanční krizi a vysoké zadlužení).</description>

<description>Tuzem&#353;tí operátoři pokračují v pokrývání železničních tratí bezdrátovým mobilním signálem.
